**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination**
- **Member:** Harper Grant
- **Member ID:** W740585624
- **Reference number:** POC-BA397EFDB1-13824
- **Date of denial notice:** August 23, 2026
- **Service denied:** Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
- **Requesting surgeon:** Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Governing policy:** Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (effective 11/15/2025), https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/small-joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

---

Dear Member Rights and Appeals:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for bunion surgery (CPT 28296), which Blue Cross and Blue Shield of North Carolina denied on August 23, 2026 on the grounds that the procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve the surgery my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that I need.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **February 19, 2027**, and I am submitting it in writing to Member Rights and Appeals at the mailing address and fax number above.

I have reviewed the guideline that applies to this request. Below I set out the plan's own published language and then the matching information from my medical records.

## The plan's criteria and the records

**1. Pain and functional limitation.** The guideline states:

> "Significant pain and functional limitation of the first metatarsophalangeal joint and/or presence of a pre-ulcer (e.g., Wagner grade 0-1) that persists after at least 12 weeks of supervised conservative management OR nonhealing ulcer at the site of the bunion or the second toe"

and defines the threshold this way:

> "For this guideline's purposes, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 3 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes."

My records document 14 months of progressive pain in the foot that is not relieved by rest. On examination, provocative testing was positive on the affected side and my range of motion is limited by pain. I cannot tolerate closed shoes, and my chart notes ulceration risk over the bony prominence. That is precisely the difficulty "walking and wearing reasonable shoes" the guideline describes. My recorded pain rating is [VAS pain score as documented by Dr. Reyes], and I am asking Dr. Reyes's office to forward that note with this appeal.

**2. Duration of conservative management.** I want to be straightforward with the reviewer about how my care maps to the 12-week period in the language quoted above, because I would rather the plan weigh the actual record than assume anything.

My supervised course of physical therapy ran 8 weeks, from May 23, 2026 to July 18, 2026, with 24 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. Conservative treatment of this condition, however, has extended well beyond that single course: I took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, I received a corticosteroid injection on June 12, 2026 that gave only about 2 weeks of partial relief, and I have used activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic. My symptoms have persisted across 14 months despite all of it.

If the plan denied this request because it counted only the 8-week supervised therapy block and not the full course of conservative care in my chart, I am asking it to look at the record as a whole. If the plan applied some other reading of this criterion, I am asking it to say so specifically in its response.

**3. The types of conservative treatment required.** The guideline states:

> "Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:"

and lists:

> "Activity modification Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics Corticosteroid injection(s) Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses"

My records satisfy both halves of this requirement, and not narrowly. For the first half, I had footwear modification (wide toe-box footwear) **and** an accommodative device (a custom orthotic). For the second half, my chart documents three of the four listed complementary strategies, not the one the policy asks for: activity modification, anti-inflammatory medication (NSAIDs for 8 months), and a corticosteroid injection on June 12, 2026.

The guideline also states:

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate. If conservative management is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such an approach is not reasonable."

My compliance is documented: 24 completed physical therapy visits over 8 weeks, with a discharge note, plus 8 months of medication use. I did the conservative treatment, consistently, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

**4. Radiographic confirmation.** The guideline states:

> "Radiographic confirmation of an elevated hallux valgus angle (HVA) (metatarsophalangeal angle greater than 15 degrees or intermetatarsal angle greater than 9 degrees)"

This criterion is met, and by a wide margin. My weight-bearing foot radiographs of June 27, 2026 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees. The plan's threshold is greater than 15 degrees for the metatarsophalangeal angle; mine is 38. The plan's threshold is greater than 9 degrees for the intermetatarsal angle; mine is 17. The policy asks for one of the two. My films show both.

**5. Imaging format and reporting.** The guideline states:

> "Where applicable, radiographic imaging must include weight-bearing anterior-posterior and lateral views of the affected foot."

My imaging was obtained weight-bearing, as the guideline requires, on June 27, 2026 — well within the window described in this provision:

> "Imaging report – The provider shall submit a detailed imaging report for studies obtained within the past 12 months. In the absence of a detailed report, the provider may submit a report from an independent radiologist."

The guideline further states:

> "Imaging reports should describe the presence or absence of subchondral cysts, subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint subluxation, or avascular necrosis. The degree of joint space narrowing should also be noted."

and:

> "Where applicable, the requesting provider should measure and record the key angular deformity indices in the medical record."

The angular deformity indices are measured and recorded in my record, as set out above. If the plan needs the full narrative radiology report addressing each of the findings listed in that provision, I am requesting that Dr. Reyes's office submit the complete imaging report from the June 27, 2026 study: [complete radiology report, to be attached]. If a documentation gap of this kind was the basis for the denial, I would ask that it be resolved by requesting the report rather than by denying the surgery.

**6. Vascular perfusion.** The guideline states:

> "Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses)"

I am asking Dr. Reyes's office to supply the vascular examination finding from my chart: [pedal pulse / vascular perfusion findings as documented by Dr. Reyes]. My records do document that I am a non-smoker with a BMI of 29 and no active infection.

**7. Clinical notes.** The guideline states:

> "Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented."

Each element of this is in my file: symptom duration (14 months, progressive, unrelieved by rest); severity and functional limitation (positive provocative testing, range of motion limited by pain, inability to tolerate closed shoes, ulceration risk over the prominence); and the type and duration of every therapeutic measure, with dates — 8 weeks and 24 visits of supervised therapy from May 23 to July 18, 2026; 8 months of NSAIDs; a corticosteroid injection on June 12, 2026; footwear modification; and a custom orthotic.

## A note on the excerpts I was able to review

One of the provisions I quoted above ends in a colon and introduces further conditions that are not reproduced in the material available to me, so the policy may contain additional requirements I have not seen. My denial notice states only that the request "does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity," without identifying which criterion was not met. **I am asking the plan to identify, specifically, which criterion of the Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery it applied and what evidence it found missing.** If it is a documentation item such as the full imaging report or the vascular examination, I am glad to have my surgeon send it; I cannot address a gap that has not been named.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Blue Cross and Blue Shield of North Carolina to:

1. Overturn the denial dated August 23, 2026 (reference POC-BA397EFDB1-13824) and authorize bunion surgery, CPT 28296;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with relevant expertise who has the complete record, including the physical therapy discharge note, the June 27, 2026 weight-bearing radiographs and report, and Dr. Reyes's clinical notes;
3. If the denial is maintained, state in writing the specific criterion from the guideline named above that my records do not meet, and tell me what further documentation or review rights are available to me.

I have followed the conservative treatment plan my doctors recommended, over 14 months, and my symptoms have not resolved. My surgeon has documented that this surgery is needed. I would appreciate the plan's careful reconsideration, and I am happy to provide anything further that would help.

Thank you for your time and attention.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Harper Grant**
